job_description_info.job_description:
# Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform

**Company:** Halden Pay (fictional name; cross-border business payments)
**Location:** Lisbon, Portugal (hybrid, 3 days per week in the office)
**Team:** Data Platform

## The role

Halden Pay is growing quickly, and data sits at the centre of that plan. We are looking for a Senior Data Engineer to join the Data Platform team. The team builds and runs the shared data platform that analysts, data scientists and product teams rely on, with a focus on reusable frameworks rather than one-off pipelines.

## Responsibilities

- Own the design, build and day-to-day running of the company's central data platform
- Evaluate and introduce new open-source tools where they bring a clear benefit
- Work with data scientists, analytics engineers and BI colleagues to turn their needs into platform features
- Define and enforce data quality standards, governance rules and access policies

## Tech stack

- Cloud: Google Cloud (BigQuery, Cloud Run, GKE)
- Orchestration and transformation: Airflow, dbt
- Engineering: Python, SQL, Docker, CI/CD, Git

## Requirements

- Experience designing, building and operating production data platforms or cloud data warehouses at scale
- Advanced Python and SQL, including query optimisation on large datasets
- Strong data modelling skills (dimensional modelling; graph modelling is a plus)
- Hands-on experience with Google Cloud or a comparable cloud (managed warehouse, serverless compute, containers)
- Curiosity about new data architecture ideas and open-source practices
- Good professional English; Portuguese is a plus

If you meet most but not all of the points above, you are still welcome to apply.

## Benefits

- Base salary plus annual bonus
- Training and certification budget
- Support for open-source contributions
- Hybrid work from a central Lisbon office

Tiago Ferrão-Lindqvist
Test & Validation Engineer (Mechanical)

Setúbal, Portugal - tiago.ferraolindqvist@example.com - +351 555 010 311 - linkedin.com/in/tfl-example

Profile
Mechanical engineer with 12 years in product design and test & validation of automotive and industrial components. I write Python and MATLAB tools that turn test-rig data into reports and engineering decisions, and I want to move into data engineering.

Experience

Test & Validation Engineer, Corvane Automotive Components (seat structures and seat-adjuster mechanisms), Setúbal - Mar 2019 to present
- Plan and run durability, vibration and climatic tests on seat-adjuster mechanisms across 6 servo-hydraulic and electric test rigs; write the test reports sent to OEM customers.
- Wrote Python scripts (pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib) that read the rig output files, check every channel against the test specification and produce the standard report figures; report preparation went from about 3 days to half a day per test.
- Correlate rig results with FEA (ANSYS Mechanical) and lead root-cause analysis (8D) on field failures; the redesigned adjuster rail bracket I proposed cut warranty returns for that part by 40%.
- Query the plant's test-results database (SQL Server) for trend analysis across three product generations.
- Maintain MATLAB/Simulink models of the adjuster drive, used to choose rig load profiles.

Mechanical Design Engineer, Halvik Pumps (industrial centrifugal pumps), Porto - Sep 2014 to Feb 2019
- Designed pump casings and impellers in SolidWorks; production drawings with GD&T; DFMEA owner for two product lines.
- Structural FEA of casings in ANSYS; moved one casing family from grey cast iron to ductile iron, saving 12% material cost.
- Supported the conversion of the pump performance test bench to a PLC-controlled setup (Siemens S7).

Education
MSc Mechanical Engineering, Sado Valley Polytechnic, 2014
Thesis: Fatigue life prediction of welded brackets under variable-amplitude loading

Skills
Python (pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib), MATLAB/Simulink, SQL, ANSYS Mechanical, SolidWorks, CATIA V5, LabVIEW, Minitab, design of experiments (DOE), GD&T, DFMEA, 8D problem solving, Excel/VBA, Power BI

Languages
Portuguese (native), English (fluent), Spanish (good)

company_info.company_description:
Halden Pay is a fintech serving exporters with business accounts, foreign-exchange risk management and trade-finance services. Its work spans areas including payments, risk, data and client experience.

The company’s stated values are **Together, Ownership and Pace**: sharing context and helping across teams, taking responsibility and learning from mistakes, and simplifying work so it can move quickly for clients. Halden Pay offers career paths, an annual learning budget and departmental mentoring. Most offices follow a hybrid model, typically with three days in the office, and team events help connect colleagues across roughly 40 offices.

Employee feedback describes a commercially driven workplace with friendly colleagues, though reported culture ratings are a little below those of similar-sized financial-services companies. Reviews also note that onboarding and training can vary between teams.

generated_cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform role at Halden Pay. Over 12 years in mechanical engineering, I have built practical data-processing tools and used test-results data to support reliable decisions. I am now looking to move into data engineering, bringing a strong foundation in Python, SQL and data validation.

At Corvane Automotive Components, I developed Python scripts that read test-rig output, validate every channel against specifications and generate standard report figures. This reduced report preparation from about three days to half a day per test. I also query a SQL Server database to analyse trends across three product generations. This work has taught me the value of repeatable processes, clear data checks and outputs that colleagues can use with confidence—principles that align with Halden Pay’s focus on shared, reusable platform frameworks and data quality.

My experience has been in engineering data rather than operating a cloud data platform. I would bring to the Data Platform team hands-on Python and SQL experience, a disciplined approach to validating data, and a track record of improving a recurring workflow. Halden Pay’s emphasis on ownership and simplifying work to move quickly also resonates with the way I approach engineering problems: identify the source of an issue, develop a practical improvement and verify its impact.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to Halden Pay’s data platform and its users across analytics, data science and product teams. Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Tiago Ferrão-Lindqvist

The Python automation achievement, 40% reduction in warranty returns, and 12% material-cost saving provide credible impact. The progression from mechanical design to test and validation is easy to follow, and the document is appropriately tailored toward a data-engineering transition without claiming unsupported cloud or platform experience. The main content limitation is that it presents engineering-data experience well but does not establish senior data-platform ownership, production operations, or data architecture experience required by this role.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly: it uses standard section headings, chronological experience, conventional bullet points, readable dates, and no tables, graphics, columns, or unusual formatting. Relevant terms such as Python, pandas, NumPy, SQL Server, MATLAB/Simulink, data processing, trend analysis, validation, and report generation are present. critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with Python-based engineering data processing, SQL Server analysis, data validation, automation, reporting, and professional English. Portuguese is also clearly shown as a plus. The strongest transferable evidence is the Python pipeline that reads test-rig files, validates channels against specifications, generates reports, and reduces preparation time from about three days to half a day. However, the candidate's material does not show experience designing, building, or operating production data platforms or cloud data warehouses at scale; advanced SQL involving query optimisation on large datasets; dimensional or graph modelling; Google Cloud or a comparable cloud; or open-source/data-architecture work. The document should therefore position the candidate as an experienced engineer transitioning toward data engineering, not as an established senior data-platform engineer. No unsupported company-culture claims or technical skills have been added.

COVER LETTER

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform role at Halden Pay. Over 12 years in mechanical engineering, I have built practical data-processing tools and used test-results data to support reliable decisions. I am now looking to move into data engineering, bringing a strong foundation in Python, SQL and data validation.

At Corvane Automotive Components, I developed Python scripts that read test-rig output, validate every channel against specifications and generate standard report figures. This reduced report preparation from about three days to half a day per test. I also query a SQL Server database to analyse trends across three product generations. This work has taught me the value of repeatable processes, clear data checks and outputs that colleagues can use with confidence—principles that align with Halden Pay’s focus on shared, reusable platform frameworks and data quality.

My experience has been in engineering data rather than operating a cloud data platform. I would bring to the Data Platform team hands-on Python and SQL experience, a disciplined approach to validating data, and a track record of improving a recurring workflow. Halden Pay’s emphasis on ownership and simplifying work to move quickly also resonates with the way I approach engineering problems: identify the source of an issue, develop a practical improvement and verify its impact.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to Halden Pay’s data platform and its users across analytics, data science and product teams. Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Tiago Ferrão-Lindqvist
